paragraphs: On 24 April 1741, Broughton fought George Stevenson at his amphitheatre off Oxford Road, then on London's edge. Stevenson went down repeatedly over four rounds and died of his injuries a few days later; the rules Broughton wrote two years afterward, dated 16 August 1743, opened by outlawing exactly what had killed him.

Those seven rules gave a fallen fighter thirty seconds to rise unassisted, but matches stayed bare-knuckle. Broughton padded a fighter's fists only later, in February 1747, with leather 'mufflers' stuffed with horsehair, and only for sparring at the separate academy where he taught gentlemen who did not want to be bloodied.
